title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents) to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that deterministically validates and (when eligible) applies at most one deterministic repair to the identical initial LLM candidate improves emulator-executable success relative to ungated LLM generation. Generation used gpt-5-mini (single shared candidate per intent); the guarded arm applied a deterministic validator and a rule-based repair operator with repair_budget ≤ 1. Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995); guarded = 200/200 (1.000); contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial) on discordant counts yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 15-percentage-point target effect is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We expand the manuscript with (a) a concise algorithmic description of the deterministic repair operator and its decision rules; (b) an explicit exact-test justification for the McNemar exact-binomial implementation used; (c) representative per-task difficulty exemplars and a pointer to the archived full per-episode difficulty manifest; and (d) artifact-grounded execution accounting and reproducibility guidance. All prompts, traces, validator outputs, repair traces (the single invoked repair), and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution and analysis bundles referenced in the evidence manifest.

sections.introduction:
Automating routine NetOps changes with generative LLMs promises reduced operator effort but raises a critical operational safety question: will LLM-produced configuration artifacts execute correctly when applied to network control planes? Prior work documents hallucinations, missing or misordered commands, and unwanted protected-field modifications as recurring failure modes for structured outputs, and proposes mitigations such as constrained decoding, retrieval augmentation, verifier-assisted repair loops, and multi-stage architectures. However, end-to-end evidence quantifying the marginal effect of a bounded, deterministic repair operator applied to the same initial LLM candidate (the shared-initial-generation estimand) is limited. 

We preregistered (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) and executed a paired experiment comparing: (A) direct evaluation of a single gpt-5-mini initial candidate per intent (baseline) and (B) deterministic validation plus at most one deterministic repair applied to that identical candidate (guarded). The shared-candidate estimand isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness at low model-call cost and supports artifact-backed auditability. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation under the shared-candidate estimand; (2) exact paired counts and a prespecified exact McNemar inferential implementation appropriate for small discordant counts; and (3) a concise, auditable description of the deterministic validator and the deterministic repair operator used in the guarded pipeline, together with execution accounting and operational interpretation grounded in archived artifacts.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and prototype studies show active application of LLMs to intent-to-configuration translation, co-pilots, and NetOps assistance while repeatedly reporting structural and semantic failures for generated configurations. Cross-domain mitigations include RAG, constrained decoding and live schema grounding, verifier-assisted repair loops, and multi-stage architectures; these reduce but do not eliminate hallucinations. Formal verification approaches (e.g., NetKAT variants and ensemble verifiers) can detect reachability and isolation violations but face practical fidelity and scalability limits [doi:10.1145/3808318]. Architectural work on agentic NetOps emphasizes that operational reliability depends on surrounding assurance machinery (evidence traces, bounded tool use, rollback policies) as much as on base-model capability [https://openalex.org/W7161165783].

Our study occupies a focused point in this space: given an identical initial candidate, how much incremental yield does a low-cost, deterministic repair operator provide? This isolates cost-versus-yield trade-offs relevant to operators who may prefer a shared-candidate, low-call-cost deployment versus higher-call-budget designs that permit re-sampling or LLM-invoked repairs.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design: The experiment was preregistered prior to execution (study_id cnd-001-5f3a). Confirmatory scope: n=200 curated natural-language intents spanning single-device and small multi-device changes (VLAN/MTU updates, uplink switchover, access-transfer patterns). Each intent was evaluated in paired fashion: a single LLM generation (shared_initial_candidate) was used for both arms; the baseline arm scored that candidate directly, and the guarded arm first applied a deterministic validator and then, only when the validator reported a repairable violation family with an unambiguous mapping, applied at most one deterministic repair iteration (repair_budget ≤ 1). Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; the realized run used 201 hosted-model calls (shared generation = 200; repair-stage calls recorded = 1). The deterministic execution environment comprised Dockerized Mininet + FRR routers orchestrated by the adapter family used in the run. Inclusion/exclusion and contamination detection rules were preregistered and applied.

Deterministic validator (scientific description): the validator deterministically performs three ordered stages on the normalized candidate. Stage 1: syntactic parse and canonical normalization of CLI-like lines into a normalized_configuration and tokenized command records; parse failures are flagged SYNTAX_PARSE_ERROR. Stage 2: structural/workflow checks—presence of required commands (per-task required_sequence), ordering/dependency constraints (e.g., make-before-break, shutdown_configure_restore patterns), group-activity policies (exactly-one/minimum-active), and protected-interface enforcement; each detected problem receives a deterministic violation code (for example, MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION). Stage 3: deterministic application simulation on the emulator model to produce an observed final_state that is compared to the task’s expected_final_state. The boolean validation outcome used in the primary estimand is validation_after.valid. The validator records parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count, and violation list for every episode; these traces form the basis for repair decisions and are archived.
sections.results:
Primary outcomes: All planned episodes completed (400 episodes = 200 pairs) with zero provider/API failures. Artifact-backed counts: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (1.0). The paired contingency table is n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0, yielding a paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial) on discordant counts yields p = 1.0. Complementary uncertainty quantification used paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap seed 1729), producing CI = [0.0, 0.015]. These results and all per-episode scoring JSONL and analysis outputs are archived in the execution and analysis bundles referenced in the manuscript.

Repair and failure accounting: the validator initially flagged violation_count > 0 in exactly one confirmatory episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1, and that single deterministic repair converted the failing candidate into a validator-passing configuration producing the single guarded-only success (n10=1). Syntactic parse failures in the confirmatory set = 0. Provider-call audit recorded hosted-model calls used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200, repair-stage calls = 1). Missingness summary shows no unscorable or missing episodes. The low discordant count drives the exact McNemar outcome: with n = n10 + n01 = 1, the two-sided exact-binomial p-value equals 1.0 for the observed ordering (n10=1, n01=0); the bootstrap CI reflects sampling uncertainty under the paired resampling scheme.

Representative difficulty context: to help interpret the near-ceiling baseline we provide six representative exemplar tasks (archived with the execution bundle) with difficulty labels among them: medium=1, hard=2, very_hard=3. The full per-episode difficulty labels for all 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in the archived task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl) and are available to auditors; we do not reproduce the exhaustive per-task table inline to preserve manuscript concision and to keep the paper focused on the confirmatory estimand and primary counts.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation: under the shared-initial-generation estimand and for the curated task distribution, ungated gpt-5-mini generation produced near-perfect candidates (199/200). A bounded, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate produced a single additional pass. Two practical implications follow. First, deterministic validators supply actionable violation codes and operationally useful audit traces; they are an essential assurance component even when model quality is high. Second, when base-model generation quality is already near-ceiling for the evaluated distribution, conservative rule-based repairs applied to the same candidate yield limited marginal operational improvement while incurring minimal extra model-call cost.

Exact-test rationale and power implications: McNemar’s test for paired binary outcomes is the preregistered primary hypothesis test. For small discordant counts the exact (binomial) form is appropriate: if n = n10 + n01 denotes the number of discordant pairs, under the null each discordant pair is equally likely to fall in either direction and the count of n10 follows Binomial(n, 0.5). With observed n = 1 (n10 = 1, n01 = 0), the two-sided exact-binomial p-value equals 1.0 for the observed ordering. The bootstrap CI complements the exact test: paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (seed 1729) yields [0.0, 0.015], excluding the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target. The realized near-ceiling baseline compresses discordant counts and substantially reduces power to detect large absolute improvements targeted in the preregistration.

Design-space trade-offs and practitioner guidance: the shared-initial-generation estimand intentionally minimizes model-call cost (one generation per intent). Alternative designs can increase yield at higher cost: (a) independent-resampling per arm (separate generation for baseline and guarded) increases discordant opportunities for repair-driven gains; (b) multi-iteration deterministic repair budgets or LLM-invoked repair steps permit richer corrections but require governance for LLM repair calls; (c) richer validators (control-plane timing models, vendor-specific semantics) increase fidelity but require more detailed state modelling. The archived execution accounting reported here (hosted-model calls used = 201; repair invocations = 1) enables concrete cost-versus-yield comparisons between these designs.

Threats to validity (summary): internal validity risks include prompt sensitivity and the chosen shared-candidate estimand (it isolates on-same-candidate repair but may understate gains possible from independent re-sampling); construct validity includes whether the validator’s deterministic simulation captures all operationally relevant runtime effects; external validity: single model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic curated task bank, and a single emulator stack (Mininet+FRR) limit generalizability to multi-vendor production environments; conclusion validity: near-ceiling baseline limited discordant counts and therefore the confirmatory test’s power to detect large preregistered effects. These limitations are addressed explicitly in the Limitations section and by archiving the full execution and analysis artifacts for external re-analysis.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, autonomy-locked paired experiment evaluating whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success of LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-initial-generation estimand. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the bounded deterministic GVR pipeline (validator + ≤1 deterministic repair on the same candidate) succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) and therefore does not support the preregistered 15 percentage-point absolute-effect target because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. For the studied estimand and curated distribution, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate produced negligible marginal gain. Practitioners should treat deterministic validators as essential assurance machinery and select estimands and repair budgets (shared-candidate vs independent-resampling, bounded rule-based repair vs LLM-invoked repair) consistent with operational cost and risk constraints. Future work should evaluate independent-resampling guarded designs, multi-vendor CLI diversity, adversarial/out-of-distribution intents, larger repair budgets, and higher-fidelity control-plane emulation to determine when guarded architectures produce substantive operational improvements.

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt and autonomy boundary. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, study selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting.

Models and tooling: generation used gpt-5-mini (requested_model recorded in execution/model_configuration.json); validation used a deterministic validator (scorer recorded in scoring artifacts as deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and the scoring_rule 'full_intent_constraint_validation'); execution used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Key preregistered settings (not altered post-lock): primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; analysis plan = exact McNemar two-sided with paired-bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes (200 pairs) using 201 hosted-model calls (shared_initial_generation=200, repair-stage calls=1). All per-episode prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair), analysis artifacts, and the full execution manifest are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the manuscript (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*).
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task set focused on small single- and small multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLIs, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.

Emulator (Dockerized Mininet+FRR) and deterministic validator model control-plane behavior deterministically but do not fully capture production runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration in the confirmatory protocol; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.

Shared-initial-generation design (single initial candidate per intent shared across arms) reduced model-call cost and isolated repair effectiveness on identical candidates but reduces external generalizability compared with independent re-sampling per arm.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Full per-task difficulty label counts for all 200 confirmatory intents are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl; exhaustive per-episode difficulty counts are provided in that artifact rather than enumerated inline to preserve concise manuscript presentation while maintaining auditable reproducibility.
